conflicts.original: A teacher working without an aide never supervises more than 12 preschool children, and teachers always keep children in sight.
conflicts.planted: A teacher working without an aide may supervise up to 16 preschool children, and teachers always keep children in sight.
conflicts.why: 22 CCR 101216.3(a): one teacher may visually observe and supervise no more than 12 children; a teacher alone with 16 preschoolers exceeds the ratio (aides only raise it to 15 or 18 with a teacher and aide together).

conflicts.original: We practice a disaster drill at least every six months and keep a written record of each drill for at least one year.
conflicts.planted: We practice a disaster drill once a year and keep a written record of each drill for at least one year.
conflicts.why: 22 CCR 101174(d): disaster drills must be conducted at least every six months and documented; once a year is too infrequent.

conflicts.original: We never take away food, rest, or toileting as a consequence.
conflicts.planted: Children who throw food or leave the table during lunch may lose their afternoon snack that day.
conflicts.why: 22 CCR 101223(a)(3): children must be free from punitive actions, including interference with daily living functions such as eating; withholding a snack as a consequence is prohibited discipline (and 101223.2 bars it even with parent consent).

conflicts.original: Children are never left in a parked vehicle, even for a moment.
conflicts.planted: If children fall asleep on the drive back, they may finish their nap buckled in the parked van while a teacher checks on them from the office window.
conflicts.why: 22 CCR 101225(e): children shall not be left in parked vehicles (for infants, 101425 also requires constant adult supervision in vehicles).

conflicts.original: A teacher watches and listens to sleeping babies at all times and physically checks each sleeping baby every 15 minutes, writing down the time and their initials on the sleep log.
conflicts.planted: A teacher looks in on sleeping babies about every 30 minutes and writes the time and their initials on the sleep log.
conflicts.why: 22 CCR 101429(a)(2): sleeping infants must be directly observed by sight and sound at all times, and staff must physically check each sleeping infant every 15 minutes and document each check; 30-minute look-ins violate both.

removals.text: As required by law, signs at our entrance give the local health department's phone number and information about California's child passenger safety seat law.
Smoking is not allowed anywhere on our premises at any time.
Before every field trip, we ask you to sign and date a permission form for that specific trip.
